subject: print of a ggplot2 object isn't working

messages.author: 2c00ac9743c15fe7
messages.subject: print of a ggplot2 object isn't working
parts:
Here's my code in a function called from elsewhere:

plot.polyreg <- function(fits)  {
  
  
  library(ggplot2)
  maxdeg <- length(fits) - 2

 
dfits <- data.frame(fits$x, fits$y)
aa <- fits$x
bb <- fits$y
ggqp <- qplot(x=fits$x, y=fits$y, data=dfits, geom = "point") 
print(ggqp)
print(aa)
print(bb)
 
ggp <- ggplot(dfits, aes(x=fits$x, y=fits$y)) + geom_point()
summary(ggp)
ggp <- ggp + xlab("XX") + ylab("YY")

print(ggp)                     #This seems to blow its mind.

.
.
.
}

The qplot works, all the print and summary statements work, down to the print(ggp).  Upon execution of the print(ggp), it tells me in the debugger in the console window
that it can't find any object, and the plot is blank:

Browse[2]> plot(ggp)
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'fits' not found
Called from: top level 
Browse[3]> summary(ggqp)
Error during wrapup: object 'ggqp' not found
Browse[3]> aa
Error during wrapup: object 'aa' not found
Browse[3]> bb
Error during wrapup: object 'bb' not found
Browse[3]> maxdeg
Error during wrapup: object 'maxdeg' not found
Browse[3]> ggp
Error during wrapup: object 'ggp' not found

I am using RStudio.  In the "data values" window, all these objects appear fine. All have the right values.  But the code can't find anything.

Help!

Thanks, George

messages.subject: Re: print of a ggplot2 object isn't working
parts:
Firstly, your example is not reproducible because 'fits' wasn't
supplied, so there is no frame of reference for someone to diagnose
the problem exactly.

On Thu, Mar 13, 2014 at 3:08 PM, yosts <yo...@mindspring.com> wrote:
> Here's my code in a function called from elsewhere:
>
> plot.polyreg <- function(fits) {
>
> library(ggplot2)
> maxdeg <- length(fits) - 2

length() is normally used to indicate the number of elements of an
atomic object. If you use it in a data frame, it returns the number of
columns. The safer (and more understandable) code is ncol(fits) if
fits is indeed a data frame.
>
> dfits <- data.frame(fits$x, fits$y)

The above suggests that fits has more than one component, which means
it could be a data frame or a list.

aa and bb are repetitious and unnecessary here. The next line can be called with

gggp <- qplot(x = x, y = y, data = dfits, geom = "point")

> ggqp <- qplot(x=fits$x, y=fits$y, data=dfits, geom = "point")
> print(ggqp)
> print(aa)
> print(bb)
>

Again, when the data frame is named, you don't need to call it again
to access the variables:

ggp <- ggplot(dfits, aes(x = x, y = y)) + geom_point()

And here's the problem; you call the data frame dfits, and then try to
access fits$x and fits$y, which reside in a different object. If you
use the above line (and it reflects what you want), the problem should
disappear.
I don't know the purpose of this next line...
After you fix the above line of code, this should work..

> print(ggp) #This seems to blow its mind.
>
> .
> .
> }
>

> The qplot works, all the print and summary statements work, down to the
> print(ggp). Upon execution of the print(ggp), it tells me in the debugger
> in the console window
> that it can't find any object, and the plot is blank:
>
The error message in the first line is informative:

> Browse[2]> plot(ggp)
> Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'fits' not found
> Called from: top level
> Browse[3]> summary(ggqp)
> Error during wrapup: object 'ggqp' not found
> Browse[3]> aa
> Error during wrapup: object 'aa' not found
> Browse[3]> bb
> Error during wrapup: object 'bb' not found
> Browse[3]> maxdeg
> Error during wrapup: object 'maxdeg' not found
> Browse[3]> ggp
> Error during wrapup: object 'ggp' not found
>
> I am using RStudio. In the "data values" window, all these objects appear
> fine. All have the right values. But the code can't find anything.

It's hard to tell what type of object fits is supposed to be, but if
it's a data frame, try something like this:

plot.polyreg <- function(fits) {

require(ggplot2)
maxdeg <- ncol(fits) - 2

# If fits is a data frame, the next line may be unnecessary
# dfits <- data.frame(fits$x, fits$y)
ggqp <- qplot(x=x, y=y, data=dfits, geom = "point")
print(ggqp)
print(dfits)

ggp <- ggplot(dfits, aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_point()

.
.
.
}


Suggestion: simplify the function as much as possible. When it works,
then you can start adding other things to it. That way, if something
goes wrong, you know which code you can eliminate as potentially
problematic.

Dennis
